# v0.5.0b1 — Independent Modbus service (beta)

The optional Modbus service owns the serial adapter and maintains the wallbox
heartbeat while Home Assistant Core restarts. It holds the last requested
charging state indefinitely during HA outages, including a deliberate pause.
HA reconnects without replaying old control values.

This beta needs installation and hardware acceptance testing. Direct serial
mode remains available. Do not run both serial owners on the same adapter.

## Installation

1. Install **v0.5.0b1** of the integration. Enable the repository's **Pre-release**
   switch in the Marketplace on HA 2026.11+, or beta releases in HACS on older
   supported HA versions. The stable release remains **v0.4.1**.
2. In HA OS, add the app repository:
   `https://github.com/memphi2/ha-mennekes-amtron#apps-beta`.
3. Install **Mennekes Amtron Modbus Service**, configure its serial settings and
   private token, and follow the [handover guide](https://github.com/memphi2/ha-mennekes-amtron/blob/v0.5.0b1/docs/modbus-service.md).
4. Reconfigure the existing integration to use the service URL and token.
   Keep the existing entry to retain device and entity identities.

For HA Container, run `ghcr.io/memphi2/ha-mennekes-amtron-service:0.5.0b1`
independently, with its data volume, serial device and private network.

## Included fixes and safeguards

- Error-200 recovery preserves deliberate pause and charging-release intent.
- The repair dialog waits up to ten seconds for error 200 to clear after the
  recovery writes, avoiding a premature "fault still active" message.
- Remote resume applies HA's current cap to the service's current intent under
  the write lock, even when another client changed it after HA last polled.
- Remote write-rejection repairs update without changing unchanged entity states.
- Shared driver and write guards for direct mode and service mode.
- Authenticated, bounded API; no raw register-write or shutdown endpoint.
- State is saved only when control intent changes. Heartbeat health records
  transitions, not a continuously changing timestamp.
- Successful service commands wait for file and directory sync so a confirmed
  pause or charging-release block is durably saved.
- Native amd64/aarch64 images are tested and published before the app catalog.
- Container provenance is bound to native build digests, including on retries;
  an existing image with copied version/source labels cannot be adopted.
- Beta releases remain separate from stable installation/update channels.

A host/app restart or USB failure still interrupts heartbeat delivery and uses
the wallbox's configured fallback. Clearing error 200 while paused requires
confirmation on the actual firmware.

The GitHub release retains one HACS installation ZIP and its verification assets.
The container is distributed through GHCR, not a second ZIP.
